changed.old: This document presents a comprehensive blueprint for establishing the Laboratory for Incentivization, Coordination and Cooperation (LICC) as a jointly-sponsored research institution between the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) and the Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI). LICC will pioneer the emerging field of coordination science—the mathematical and computational study of how economic agents, institutions, and jurisdictions can be designed to achieve optimal collective outcomes through programmable incentive mechanisms.
changed.new: The Laboratory for Incentivization, Coordination and Cooperation (LICC) is proposed as a joint research institution. Its sponsors would be the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) and the Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI). Coordination science studies how economic agents, institutions, and jurisdictions can be designed for optimal collective outcomes through programmable incentive mechanisms. LICC will develop this emerging field using mathematical and computational methods.

changed.old: The convergence of cryptographic primitives, programmable compliance infrastructure, and the emergence of Special Economic Zones as innovation laboratories has created an unprecedented opportunity to establish a new academic discipline. Current institutional arrangements—from international trade to jurisdictional governance—operate on frameworks designed for a pre-digital era. LICC will develop the theoretical foundations and practical tools to design "programmable institutions" that can operate at software speed while maintaining the legitimacy and stability of traditional governance structures.
changed.new: Cryptographic primitives, programmable compliance infrastructure, and Special Economic Zones used for experimentation now support the development of a new academic discipline. Institutions governing international trade and jurisdictions still use frameworks designed before the digital era. LICC will develop the theory and tools for "programmable institutions" that operate at software speed while preserving the legitimacy and stability of traditional governance.

changed.old: This dual-sponsorship model uniquely combines MIT's world-class theoretical expertise in mechanism design, institutional economics, and network science with MBZUAI's applied AI infrastructure and direct pathways to government implementation through UAE's 27 free zones. The recently announced MIT-MBZUAI Collaborative Research Program (October 2025) provides an existing institutional framework that can be expanded to accommodate LICC's coordination science mandate.
changed.new: The dual-sponsorship model combines MIT's theoretical expertise in mechanism design, institutional economics, and network science with MBZUAI's applied AI infrastructure. MBZUAI also provides direct routes to government implementation through the UAE's 27 free zones. The MIT-MBZUAI Collaborative Research Program, announced in October 2025, provides an institutional framework that could expand to include LICC's coordination science mandate.

changed.old: 1.2 MIT: Institutional Profile and Strategic Assets
changed.new: 1.2 MIT: Institutional Profile and Research Resources

changed.old: The Massachusetts Institute of Technology represents the world's premier institution for the theoretical foundations LICC requires. MIT's research enterprise spans $2.1 billion annually, with industry-sponsored research totaling $175 million from over 300 companies in fiscal year 2024—approximately 20% of total MIT research expenditures. According to the National Science Foundation, MIT consistently ranks first or second in industry-funded research and development expenditures among universities without a medical school.
changed.new: MIT has expertise in the theoretical foundations LICC requires. MIT's research enterprise totals $2.1 billion annually. In fiscal year 2024, industry-sponsored research totaled $175 million from over 300 companies, approximately 20% of total MIT research expenditures. According to the National Science Foundation, MIT consistently ranks first or second in industry-funded research and development expenditures among universities without a medical school.

changed.old: 1.3 MBZUAI: Institutional Profile and Strategic Assets
changed.new: 1.3 MBZUAI: Institutional Profile and Research Resources

changed.old: The Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence, established in October 2019, represents the world's first graduate-level research university dedicated entirely to artificial intelligence. Located in Masdar City, Abu Dhabi, MBZUAI operates as part of the UAE Strategy for Artificial Intelligence 2031—a national initiative positioning the UAE as a global AI hub. The university is fully state-funded with sovereign wealth backing through Mubadala Investment Company.
changed.new: The Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence was established in October 2019. It is the world's first graduate-level research university dedicated entirely to artificial intelligence. Based in Masdar City, Abu Dhabi, it operates under the UAE Strategy for Artificial Intelligence 2031. This national initiative positions the UAE as a global AI hub. The university is fully state-funded, with sovereign wealth backing through Mubadala Investment Company.

changed.old: In October 2025, MIT's Schwarzman College of Computing and MBZUAI announced the MIT-MBZUAI Collaborative Research Program—a five-year agreement uniting faculty, students, and research staff from both institutions. This existing framework provides the institutional foundation upon which LICC can be built.
changed.new: In October 2025, MIT's Schwarzman College of Computing and MBZUAI announced the MIT-MBZUAI Collaborative Research Program. The five-year agreement brings together faculty, students, and research staff from both institutions. LICC could be established within this framework.

changed.old: Strategic Opening for LICC
changed.new: Adding LICC to the Collaboration

changed.old: The MIT-MBZUAI collaboration explicitly addresses "social and ethical responsibilities of computing in shaping global impact"—language that creates direct alignment with LICC's coordination science mandate. However, the current program emphasizes foundation models, robotics, and healthcare AI. LICC's positioning requires demonstrating how coordination science represents a natural fourth pillar that complements rather than competes with existing priorities.
changed.new: The MIT-MBZUAI collaboration explicitly addresses "social and ethical responsibilities of computing in shaping global impact". This aligns with LICC's coordination science mandate. The current program emphasizes foundation models, robotics, and healthcare AI. To add coordination science as a fourth research area, LICC must show how it complements these priorities and secure the current program directors' agreement.

changed.old: Three primary structural configurations exist for establishing LICC within the MIT-MBZUAI framework. Each offers distinct advantages and constraints that must be evaluated against LICC's long-term research independence requirements.
changed.new: Three structures could establish LICC within the MIT-MBZUAI framework. Each has advantages and constraints that must be assessed against LICC's long-term research independence requirements.

changed.old: Mechanism: Propose LICC as an additional research theme within the existing MIT-MBZUAI Collaborative Research Program, positioning "Coordination Science" as a fourth pillar alongside scientific discovery, human thriving, and planetary health.
